verification_note: Drafted from general knowledge of India's CERT-In directions on cyber incident reporting (direction No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In of 28 April 2022) and typical incident-report forms. Field names, the incident-type list and the timing rule have NOT been checked against the current official directions or reporting form. Verify every item below with compliance or legal, then set status to VERIFIED with verified_against and verified_on. AEGIS never submits anything: a human files the report.

reporting.deadline_basis: Counted from when the incident was noticed. AEGIS uses the first detection time and stores every timestamp in UTC.
reporting.note: Channels and addresses change; take them from the current official directions, not from this file.

fields.label: Organisation name
fields.description: Legal name of the affected organisation.

fields.label: Sector
fields.description: Sector the organisation operates in, for example IT, banking or healthcare.

fields.label: Point of contact
fields.description: Person CERT-In can contact about this report.

fields.label: Contact email
fields.description: Email address of the point of contact.

fields.label: Contact phone
fields.description: Phone number of the point of contact.

fields.label: Organisation address
fields.description: Postal address of the affected organisation.

fields.label: Type of incident
fields.description: Suggested from the rules and techniques that fired. Confirm it against the official category list.

fields.label: Date and time the incident was noticed (UTC)
fields.description: First detection time recorded by AEGIS; the reporting deadline counts from here.

fields.label: Date and time the activity started (UTC)
fields.description: Timestamp of the earliest correlated evidence event.

fields.label: Affected systems
fields.description: Assets in the incident, with their reported criticality.

fields.label: Affected accounts
fields.description: User accounts that appear in the evidence.

fields.label: Indicators observed
fields.description: IP addresses, domains and file hashes taken from the evidence events.

fields.label: Techniques observed (MITRE ATT&CK)
fields.description: Candidate techniques from the rules that fired. They are mappings, not confirmed attribution.

fields.label: Description of the incident
fields.description: Plain-language summary written from the incident story. Every sentence cites evidence; a human edits it before submission.

fields.label: Impact
fields.description: Business impact, data affected and services disrupted. AEGIS cannot judge this; a human writes it.

fields.label: Actions taken
fields.description: Containment and review steps recorded in AEGIS, including simulated response actions, marked as such.

fields.label: Current status of the incident
fields.description: Incident status and owner in AEGIS at the time of the draft.

fields.label: Evidence reference
fields.description: AEGIS incident identifier and event count, so the evidence can be produced on request.

fields.label: Anything else CERT-In should know
fields.description: Free text added by the person filing the report.

incident_types.label: Targeted scanning or probing of critical networks and systems
incident_types.note: Scanning of critical systems is commonly listed as reportable. Confirm the current wording.

incident_types.label: Unauthorised access to IT systems or data
incident_types.note: Brute force followed by a successful login is usually treated as unauthorised access.

incident_types.label: Malicious code attack, including ransomware
incident_types.note: Ransomware and malicious-code incidents are reportable in the directions as drafted here.

incident_types.label: Data breach or data leak
incident_types.note: Applies when data left the organisation or credentials were stolen. A human must confirm the data involved.

incident_types.label: Website defacement, or tampering with systems and logs
incident_types.note: Log clearing suggests tampering; confirm whether it fits this category.

incident_types.label: Denial of service or distributed denial of service
incident_types.note: AEGIS has no denial-of-service rule yet; select this manually when it applies.

incident_types.label: Other cyber security incident
incident_types.note: Fallback when no mapped category fits. A human chooses the correct category from the official list.

reportability_notes: AEGIS suggests a category from the rules and techniques that fired. It is a starting point, not a legal determination.
The obligation to report, the category and the deadline all depend on the current official directions and on facts AEGIS cannot see, such as the data involved and whether the organisation is covered.
Confirm with compliance or legal before filing, and file through the official channel: AEGIS never transmits reports.
